skill.description: Guide Claude Flow swarm orchestration with task decomposition, agent coordination, progress monitoring, and result synthesis.
skill.summary: Coordinates Claude Flow swarms from planning through final result synthesis.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, and no prompt injection text was found. It does contain real external command risk because many examples run npx claude-flow@alpha, spawn agents, monitor tasks, and write artifacts. Several static hits were markdown, JSON, JavaScript, shebang, jq, date, or workflow-status false positives.

remediation.issue: Mutable npx claude-flow@alpha commands execute external package code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact trusted Claude Flow version, document package provenance, and require explicit approval before running commands.

remediation.issue: Shell snippets pass plan-derived values into command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Validate task IDs and agent IDs, quote shell variables, and reject unexpected characters before assignment or status commands.

remediation.issue: Swarm setup and monitors can consume resources without clear limits.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run steps, user confirmation, cleanup traps, maximum duration, and maximum agent counts for every runnable script.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Alpha Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs users to run npx claude-flow@alpha. npx can fetch and execute package code, and the alpha tag is mutable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are direct npx invocations using the mutable @alpha tag. This is a clear supply-chain and remote code execution risk if run without approval.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Swarm Resource Usage
semantic_findings.description: The workflow spawns many agents and starts long-running monitors. Without explicit user limits, this can consume compute, tokens, and project resources unexpectedly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines spawn multiple agent types and run background monitoring loops. The behavior is documented, but resource limits and consent checks are not specified.

content.value_statement: Large development tasks are hard to split, assign, and monitor across agents. This skill provides a phased Claude Flow process for planning, execution, monitoring, and synthesis.
actual_capabilities: Breaks complex work into phased task trees with dependency checks.
Selects a swarm topology based on planned task count.
Defines coordinator and specialist agent roles for Claude Flow.
Assigns tasks after dependency status checks.
Tracks progress, blocked tasks, agent health, and workload metrics.
Collects, groups, validates, reports, and archives orchestration results.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow to be installed and configured separately.
Includes shell command examples that need review before execution.
Does not verify task security, package trust, or project policy compliance.
Can create many agents and long-running monitors if limits are not adjusted.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a large application build
use_cases.description: Plan architecture, backend, frontend, infrastructure, testing, and review work across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent workflow execution
use_cases.description: Use the phase checklist to keep decomposition, assignment, monitoring, and synthesis consistent across projects.

use_cases.title: Review swarm execution quality
use_cases.description: Collect progress metrics, blocked tasks, final outputs, and performance targets after a multi-agent run.

prompt_templates.title: Decompose a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to decompose this task into phases, dependencies, and suggested agent roles: [task].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Swarm Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Flow swarm plan for [project]. Include topology, coordinators, specialist agents, dependencies, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor Active Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define monitoring steps for the active swarm. Focus on completion rate, blocked tasks, agent health, and progress reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Synthesize Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this swarm state: [status]. Recommend recovery actions, final result collection, synthesis groups, validation checks, and report contents.

output_examples.input: Plan a full-stack application build with multiple agent roles.
output: A phased task tree covering architecture, backend, frontend, infrastructure, and testing.
Agent assignments for coordinators, researchers, coders, reviewers, and testers.
Validation checkpoints for dependencies, progress, and final synthesis.

output_examples.input: Monitor a swarm that may have blocked work.
output: A progress summary with completed, active, pending, blocked, and failed task counts.
A blocker review focused on stale tasks, dependency failures, and unresponsive agents.
Recommended follow-up actions for reassignment, retry, or escalation.

output_examples.input: Synthesize results after a multi-agent run.
output: Grouped results by architecture, implementation, and testing phases.
A final validation checklist for completeness and data loss risks.
A report outline with metrics, timeline, outputs, and unresolved issues.

best_practices: Review every shell command before running it in a project workspace.
Set explicit agent, duration, and output limits before orchestration starts.
Validate dependencies and final outputs before accepting synthesized results.
anti_patterns: Do not run unpinned package commands in sensitive repositories without approval.
Do not spawn large swarms before defining task scope and success criteria.
Do not treat synthesized output as correct without human review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan, run, monitor, and summarize Claude Flow multi-agent orchestration workflows.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples and process guidance that a user or agent may choose to run.

faq.question: Which tools does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Claude Flow workflows and is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm package trust, project permissions, agent limits, output paths, and any organization approval rules.

faq.question: Can it recover blocked tasks?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for detecting blockers and reassigning or retrying stalled work.

faq.question: Is final output guaranteed to be correct?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends validation, but users must review synthesized results and project changes.
